## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

<section class="odv-am-card" id="part-1-2-3"><div class="odv-am-img wide"><span class="odv-am-assetbox"><img class="odv-am-asset" src="/anatomy/dense-data/select/card-1.png" alt="Trigger: 1, 2, 3" loading="lazy"/></span></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">1</i><i class="odv-am-n">2</i><i class="odv-am-n">3</i><b>Trigger</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="What holds this?">Containment</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you act on it?">Affordance</span><span class="odv-am-role" title="Can you read it?">Readability</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Spacing · How dense is the layout? → Compact</div><div class="odv-am-why">Compact spacing shows more records.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Typography · How large is body text? → Small</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small body text fits more rows on the screen.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Shape · What should control corners say? → Slightly rounded</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small corners keep dense rows straight.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For field label or column header, use type.label. Don't use type.heading.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Headers repeat on every column; a heavy style would compete with the data.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For the smallest clickable thing, use size.control.compact. Don't use anything smaller.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Compact still fits a mouse. Touch is not this product's input.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For corners of buttons and inputs, use radius.control. Don't use radius.round.</div><div class="odv-am-why">Small corners keep dense rows straight.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>size.control.default</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.height</code><span class="odv-am-val">2rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> size.32</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>space.inset.control-x</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.padding-x</code><span class="odv-am-val">0.75rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> space.12</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>radius.control</code><span>→</span><code>trigger.radius</code><span class="odv-am-val">0.125rem</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The quietest text.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.600: the quietest text that still reads, 6.66:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.400: the quietest text that still reads, 6.47:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `select`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy dense-data select`
